A1.justification: Both PDFs describe An Odd Estimator for Shapley Values. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original evaluations on eight value functions, including estimation errors, runtimes, and interaction-sparsity ablations.

after.justification: The original empirical evaluation is retained and expanded with additional comparators, sampling and proxy-parameter ablations, and spectral-energy analysis.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the specified higher-order support size from ceil(m/eta) to ceil(m/eta)-d, counting the d linear terms within the regression-variable budget. The paired-sampling, GBT-screening, Fourier-regression pipeline and low-budget fallback remain intact.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight value functions: DistilBERT, Estate, ViT16, Cancer, CG60, IL60, NHANES, and Crime. The added analyses use these retained tasks and domains without introducing new data coverage.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates FourierSHAP, FFD-RD, and its corrected variant in benchmark and runtime comparisons. Proxy, already evaluated in v1's plots, also enters Tables 1 and 3. PolySHAP-3 matches the earlier 3-PolySHAP rather than constituting a new comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds paired/non-paired sampling crossed with all/odd interaction controls, tree-depth and tree-count sweeps, and SPEX spectral recovery with 100,000 queries. Tables 1 and 3 also revise reported budgets, including DistilBERT from 1,591 to 1,440. The main 30-instance evaluation, ground-truth construction, and MSE metric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained runtime and interaction-count analyses, Section 5.4 and Appendices D.4–D.6 test the contributions of pairing and odd-only selection, sensitivity to proxy capacity, and interaction spectra underlying FFD performance differences. These substantially broaden examination of the method's mechanisms and robustness.

E5.justification: Existing MSE and runtime results retain median/IQR reporting, and Table 3 retains means and quartiles. However, v2's new Figure 16 includes error bars whose statistical meaning is unspecified. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether this introduces a different uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 3 replace OddSHAP values and several NHANES baseline scores, alongside substantial new comparator and analysis results. Estate OddSHAP mean MSE changes from 6.1e-5 to 5.1e-7, but its reported budget and support rule also change, preventing a same-setting improvement interpretation. New findings include FFD-RD outperforming OddSHAP on several tree-based benchmarks.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 now distinguishes the decomposable vector space from affine boundary-constrained classes and explicitly assumes symmetric weights. Appendices B–C expand derivations and correct the regression sum and affine-projection description. Section 4 revises Fourier-extraction complexity from O(Ntrees*2^L*L) to O(Ntrees*4^L). These refine existing theory without adding a new principal theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and discussion qualify state-of-the-art accuracy as applying at larger or sufficient sampling budgets, narrowing v1's broader performance claims. Consistency, odd-only regression, and the explanation of paired sampling remain the central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains FFD's domain-dependent performance through interaction spectra and interprets the new sampling and proxy ablations. Its limitations explicitly discuss cubic scaling in the sampling budget, recommend capping interaction counts, and explain why paired sampling need not outperform independent sampling, substantially extending v1's brief coherence and correlation caveats.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the supplementary-code statement with a public repository link, specifies the default 100 LightGBM trees, and documents odd-target computation using m/2 regression rows and the affine solver shift. Exact boundary constraints, sampling-library information, and hardware were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: Section 3 now explicitly credits earlier odd-order dependence results, including newly cited Wendler and Zhou, and attributes basis equivalence to prior work. Appendix D.6 substantially develops the relationship between OddSHAP's adaptive screening and Zhou's fractional factorial designs, materially refining the positioning of the paper's central ideas.

P1.justification: The overall organization and much of the prose remain. v2 revises the introductory framing and discussion, expands regression explanations, moves Observation 3.1's proof to Appendix B, and adds experimental subsections. Affiliations, publication information, and bibliography formatting also receive localized edits.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 gain comparator rows and reorder the synthetic-data columns; benchmark and runtime plots gain traces and legends. New Figures 5 and 13–16 display sampling ablations, proxy sensitivity, and spectra. The sparsity plots relabel their horizontal axis as regression variables, while existing displays are also relocated.

improvement.justification: The added FFD/FourierSHAP comparisons and direct component ablations address substantial gaps in v1's validation. v2 acknowledges competing-method wins, qualifies its headline accuracy claim, and improves mathematical precision, prior-work attribution, and implementation documentation. Figure 16's undefined error bars remain a reporting weakness, but the gains in evidential support and accuracy of positioning are substantial.
